newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bull run seen for Hong Kong H-shares.
newsitem.headline: Bull run seen for Hong Kong H-shares.

text.p: A strong response to initial public offerings (IPO) by Beijing North Star Co Ltd and Zhejiang Expressway Co Ltd could signal a bull run for the H shares of Hong Kong-listed Chinese enterprises, analysts said.
"The recent strong performance of H-shares has reflected the fact that the sector has bottomed out and has started a new bull run," said Percy Au-young, director of research at DBS Securities.
"Their IPO responses are seen to be strong."
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises H-shares index has risen 4.97 percent since the beginning of May to hit 1,120.45 by the market close on Friday.
H share companies are firms incorporated in Hong Kong but controlled from mainland China.

The reception given to the IPOs shows "that investors are regaining confidence in the H-shares sector and are beginning to tap the bull run of the sector," said Pamela Lam, analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities.
Analysts expect China property player Beijing North Star to be oversubscribed 500 to 600 times and Zhejiang Expressway by about 300 to 400 times.
The grey market price of Zhejiang Expressway was about HK$3.50 per share and Beijing North Star was about HK$4.50 at the close of their IPO applications on Friday, analysts said.
The difference in the subscription response showed that investors favoured firms with strong parent backing, they said.
Beijing North Star attractive because its parent connection gives access to high quality development projects, analysts said.
Beijing North Star, the property arm of the Beijing municipal government, issued 614.8 million H-shares at HK$2.40 each in a public offering.

"Being granted full support from the Beijing municipal government, the company commands an unrivalled competitive edge in the property development industry in Beijing," said Patrick Chia, head of research of China Everbright Research.

The issue included 92.22 million shares offered to the public in Hong Kong, 351.48 million shares placed internationally and 171.10 million shares offered to Rich Funds Ltd, a unit of the New World Development Co Ltd.
The investment by New World Development was seen providing reassurance for other investors that Beijing North Star would have a positive earnings outlook, analysts said.

Beijing North Star's investment properties include the Asian Games Village at the centre of Beijing, consisting of a convention centre, a four-star hotel, commercial and residential blocks, and an office tower.
But uncertainty over China's property market, due to oversupply of office and residential space, could limit the long term upside potential of the shares, some analysts warned.
"The outlook for the (China) property sector is not very optimistic," Au-young said.
Dealing in its shares is expected to begin on May 14.

China toll road operator Zhejiang Expressway Co Ltd, which is controlled by the Zhejiang provincial government, issued 1.25 billion H shares in its flotation at prices ranging from HK$2.06 to HK$2.38 each.
Of the total, 124.68 million H shares are offered to the Hong Kong public, and 1.12 billion will be placed internationally.
The company builds and manages toll roads and other infrastructure in Zhejiang province.

"We expect it (Zhejiang Expressway) to have about 30 percent upside from its issue price as the company offers its shares at a discount to NAV (net asset value) and we expect it to trade at about 10 percent premium to NAV," Au-young said.
Dealing in the firm shares is expected to start on May 15.
